$comment: The risk tier of a diff, keyed by the trigger headings of .claude/skills/pr-review/checklist.md. Checked by scripts/check-review-tiers.mjs (npm run check:review-tiers; CI runs it), which fails BOTH on a heading with no row and on a row naming a heading that no longer exists -- the bidirectional shape check:root-scripts uses. This file is a declared copy of those headings, kept honest by that gate rather than by a comment. Spec: docs/specs/tiered-pr-review.spec.md (WS2, barwise-1037). Consumers read it through scripts/lib/review-tiers.mjs; two parsers over one table is the copy the rule forbids. A file-shaped glob (one naming a file, like CLAUDE.md) also fails the gate when same-named tracked files exist that its row does not reach, unless the row's reachAcknowledged lists exactly those paths under that file name, one entry per name however many of the row's globs share it (docs/specs/review-tier-reach.spec.md, barwise-1046).

tiers.always: Applies to every pull request; not a path trigger.
tiers.high-risk: Liability concentrates here -- rework across downstream packages, or external harm through a shipped surface. WS4 blocks merge on these.
tiers.routine: CI and the ratchets carry it. No blocking review.
tiers.not-path-derivable: The checklist trigger is semantic, not path-shaped. The classifier CANNOT detect it, and saying so is the point: these stay with the deep review, and a row exists so the completeness gate still accounts for the heading.

trivial.why: A pull request is trivial only if EVERY change is an EDIT (files API status modified) to one of these paths, and a trivial PR gets no Copilot review (.github/workflows/copilot-review.yml). Measured over the 60 merged PRs #466..#532 (first-parent merges ending at 2f231119): 11 (18%) changed only .beads/issues.jsonl, every one of them as an edit, and nothing else was plausibly trivial. The exact file, not .beads/: that directory also holds tracked, executable git hooks, which no measurement covered. Documentation is deliberately NOT here: PR #532 was docs-and-tracker only and a Copilot review found five real defects in it, the worst a spec diagram describing an implementation that no longer existed. The command that reproduces the count is in docs/specs/tiered-pr-review.spec.md, WS1. Widen this list only with the same kind of evidence, because a wrong entry is a defect nobody looks at.

rows.heading: Every PR
rows.why: the group with no trigger -- spec named, tracking issue open, numbers carry commands, session review present

rows.heading: When a surface changed (CLI, MCP, VS Code)
rows.why: external harm: these are what ships to users, and the capability matrix goes stale silently

rows.heading: When `@barwise/core` changed
rows.why: rework: eleven downstream packages absorb a bad decision here (root CLAUDE.md). src/ and the exports map, not the whole package -- a change to core's own tests is the tests row, and measured over the last 40 merged PRs the wider glob made 4 of 13 core triggers reach nothing under src/ (tests, core's CLAUDE.md, mutation configs). The package.json half has fired 0 times in that window and is reasoning rather than measurement. Its reach is acknowledged: the other package.json files are not core's exports map, so the row deliberately does not reach them

rows.heading: When a type was introduced, or a field's type chosen
rows.why: triggers on what a hunk does, not where it lives; any .ts file can introduce a type

rows.heading: When a module, function, or interface was introduced, or a signature widened
rows.why: same shape: a widened signature is invisible to a path matcher

rows.heading: When a copy was added or a copy was edited
rows.why: a must-agree copy is a relation between two files, which no single-path glob expresses

rows.heading: When generated output changed
rows.why: drift tests already fail when output disagrees with its regenerator

rows.heading: When tests changed
rows.why: coverage thresholds and the mutation pass carry weakening; the deep review still runs its failure-mode checks

rows.heading: When a check, gate, hook, or script was added or changed
rows.why: this is the verification apparatus itself; a gate that stops answering is the failure this repo keeps finding (barwise-906, six occurrences)

rows.heading: When a spec was added or revised
rows.why: audit:specs guards the Status claim; the rest is judgment the deep review applies

rows.heading: When an ADR changed
rows.why: a changed decision is rework for everything that follows it, and only review can tell a changed decision from a reflow

rows.heading: When Python was touched
rows.why: dev-time only and never a runtime dependency (root CLAUDE.md); check:python-uv holds the lockfile discipline

rows.heading: When a skill, agent brief, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, or prompt artifact changed
rows.why: instructions are logic: a rule change is a behaviour change with no test, and nothing else reviews it. The per-package CLAUDE.md files are named explicitly because `CLAUDE.md` is an exact path that matches only the root one -- 8 of the 13 package instruction files reached this row through no glob at all, and the other 5 only incidentally, via the surface or Python rows (WS3)

rows.heading: When a dependency was added
rows.why: external harm, supply-chain shaped. The LOCKFILES, not the manifests: a dependency change is always written into the lock by npm install or uv lock, and CI rejects a lock that disagrees with its manifest -- while a manifest edit on its own is almost always an npm script. Measured (WS3): over the last 20 merged PRs the manifest globs fired 5 times and 4 were npm script additions with no lockfile change; over 40, 7 of 8. Still makes every dependabot PR blocking, roughly five a week.

failureModes.heading: Input dropped at a boundary
failureModes.why: importers, exporters, loaders, serializers, mappers, the LLM output parser, the lineage manifest and argument parsing: the sites of REVIEW.md failure mode 1's cited defects (c3e8bd75, b0f408dc, aaf5837c, barwise-tn4)

failureModes.heading: A gate answers without seeing its input
failureModes.why: the gates, hooks, workflows and scripts themselves, the same paths as the checklist's gate row (REVIEW.md failure mode 2)

failureModes.heading: A test that cannot fail
failureModes.why: changed tests fire on 21 of the last 40 PRs (barwise/scripts/tests/, packages/*/tests/, optimizer/tests/, trial/tests/), more than half, so by review-routing WS2's rule it is always rather than routed (REVIEW.md failure mode 3)

failureModes.heading: Wired in one place, not its siblings
failureModes.why: bundle entries, surface commands and tools, format registrations, and npm scripts, each of which has siblings (REVIEW.md failure mode 4). The root package.json is the generated npm-script forwarder (scripts/regen-root-package.mjs), the sibling of barwise/package.json's scripts. The twelve package manifests are acknowledged rather than reached: the forwarder runs npm --prefix barwise, so their scripts are not forwarded

failureModes.heading: A restated fact went stale
failureModes.why: a message, doc or tool description naming a fact can live in any file (REVIEW.md failure mode 5)

failureModes.heading: Boundary text
failureModes.why: SQL and identifier handling (REVIEW.md failure mode 6)

failureModes.heading: ORM shape
failureModes.why: the model and every place that walks roles or builds ids: the sites of REVIEW.md failure mode 7's cited defects (bb9b4660 in mapping, 35ee5c4a in the importers and dbtMapping)

failureModes.heading: PR description claims
failureModes.why: every PR has a description whose claims must match the code (REVIEW.md failure mode 8)
